about: Real traffic recorded in the soft lab (lab/softlab): 1-second excerpts of the tool port (and of the broker's lossless copy, to prove fixes on real traffic). Each test set up one fault on a software switch and packet broker carrying real HTTP, HTTPS, DNS and iperf3 traffic.

cases.name: softlab_L02
cases.label: Real traffic: receive-only SPAN
cases.setup: The tool is fed by a SPAN session that copies only what the switch receives on the client port, so the server's replies never reach it.

cases.name: softlab_L04
cases.label: Real traffic: SPAN destination overloaded
cases.setup: Both directions of a busy link are mirrored into a SPAN destination port too slow for them: it discards what does not fit.

cases.name: softlab_L07
cases.label: Real traffic: packet slicing at 128 bytes
cases.setup: The packet broker slices every frame on the tool port to 128 bytes, so the IDS loses the payload it inspects.

cases.name: softlab_L08
cases.label: Real traffic: ERSPAN still wrapped
cases.setup: The switch sends an ERSPAN session to the broker, which forwards it to the tool without stripping the tunnel headers. The extra 50 bytes also push full-size frames over the IDS port's 1518-byte limit.
